question.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Exponential is Compared to Zero or a Negative Number
question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the exponential term:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4-{e}^{3x} & >2 \\ -{e}^{3x} & >6 \\ {e}^{3x} & <-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall that a positive number raised to any real power is always positive. Since $e>0,$ we have

$$
{e}^{3x}>0
$$

for every real value of $x.$

Therefore, ${e}^{3x}$ cannot be less than $-6.$ Hence, the inequality

$$
{e}^{3x}<-6
$$

has no solutions.
